elements.element: No MFN (most-favoured-nation) obligation imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: Clause 7.2 ("Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.") is deleted in its entirety by operation 1 (delete_paragraph p0027).

elements.element: MFN pricing running in Customer's favour remains permissible (nothing bars a Vendor-granted MFN)
elements.evidence: No new prohibition added; remaining text only confirms "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer ... commitment."

elements.element: Any MFN is limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation survives at all; the deleted 7.2 referenced "any other technology supplier" with no product limit and no substitute scope language was inserted.

elements.element: Any MFN is limited to a 12-month duration
elements.evidence: No duration term appears anywhere; 7.2 was removed rather than time-limited.
No comparison or carve-out language inserted; redlined output contains only "12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing..."

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully achieved: the sole Customer-side MFN covenant (7.2) is deleted, leaving no MFN burden on Customer, while Vendor-granted MFN pricing remains permissible.
Fallback elements (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) are unmet, but that is immaterial because the preferred bargain is satisfied and the two levels are not combined.

Minimality holds notwithstanding the official whole-paragraph gate: clause 7.2 consists of a single sentence that is entirely the offending MFN obligation, so no operator, number, or short phrase edit could suffice; nothing else was touched and no new exception, defined term, or dangling mechanic was introduced.
Untouched terms remain effective; the surviving § 12.3 acknowledgement that Customer has made "no ... most-favoured-customer ... commitment" is now consistent rather than contradictory.
